- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp spike in forecast (e.g., >30% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 20–30% above recent peak.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >20% above recent 18d average, adjust downward by 15–25% unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; increase forecast by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.  
- For horizon >15 days, model often underestimates true price; apply 10–15% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
